items: New: Prompt flow. Write a big task and we split it into chained steps, with parallel branches, a ready prompt for each step and the best AI for each one.
AI features can run on Claude, with a monthly spending cap: when it runs out or AI isn't available, everything keeps working on Promptea's own engine.
Chinese AI Daily stories show their real reading time, and the weekly digest shows its Chinese titles.
Fixes: the daily alert is no longer lost when sending fails, and the newsletter refuses example addresses such as name@example.com.
AI Daily can now be published in Chinese: each new story that comes with a Chinese version gets its own page under /zh. Earlier stories stay in English with a notice.
Kimi K3.1 Pro arrives in the analyzer and becomes the default Kimi; Kimi K3 moves to previous version.
We reviewed all of /zh: links, metadata and text. The newsletter form no longer shows an English email example there.
Behind the scenes: a daily check warns us if any automated publication (AI Daily, AI Daily Tech, the weekly digest or the newsletter) falls behind.
The newsletter no longer goes to test addresses that bounced.
Promptea in Simplified Chinese (/zh): the interface, the analyzer, the DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, GLM, MiniMax and Doubao pages, the glossary and the most-read guides.
The analyzer understands prompts written in Chinese and scores them the same from any interface language.
The X feed on the home page is our own: no third-party widget, lighter, and no outside scripts.
The newsletter card shows up for every visitor who has not closed it, without covering the editor or the buttons. Close it and it comes back in 7 days.
Benchmarks: every model opens its own analysis (rank in each benchmark, where it stands out, limits and price), and you can compare up to four models.
Four new AI families in the analyzer: Qwen (Alibaba Cloud), GLM (Z.ai / Zhipu AI), MiniMax and Doubao (ByteDance), each with its verified models, its own prompting rules, a model page and a guide.
The prompt analyzer explains what it checks, answers common questions and shows before → after examples with the exact scores it gives.
The most-read guides link to the analyzer, and each model page links to its guide.
New stories and guides are announced to Bing and other search engines (IndexNow) as soon as they are published.
Guide templates have a Copy button.
Security update of the site's framework (Next.js 16.4): four critical vulnerabilities closed, and pages load less JavaScript.
Better contrast in the Aqua theme: the blue of buttons, links and labels is slightly deeper and easy to read (WCAG AA).
Two new guides: AI prompts for customer feedback analysis, and for proposals and RFP responses, in English, Spanish and Portuguese.
The structured data of the benchmarks page is now valid for Google.
Update of the library that sends the newsletter.
The scrollable prompt boxes on guides, model pages, the glossary and the prompt packs can now be focused and scrolled with the keyboard.
Model catalog updated from official documentation: Claude Fable 5.2, Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 4 Carbon join. Claude Fable 5.1 becomes legacy, and old links keep working.
AI Daily Tech is not offered to search engines until it publishes its first story.
Security update of the validation library.

changelog.olderNotice: Versions before v1.8.0 are listed in English.

items: New: AI Daily Tech. One technology story a day for people who build with AI — cloud platforms, web frameworks, developer tools, hardware — with its sources, in its own section and with its own RSS feed.
AI Daily now has three tabs: AI, Tech and the weekly digest. The weekly digest gains a "Tech this week" block.
New page: how we choose and verify sources — the three tiers, what a story needs before it is published and who we read.
The home page and most pages load faster: they are now prepared in advance instead of being built on every visit.
The X feed card no longer shows a third party's error message, and it loads after the page is ready.
Prompt packs no longer scroll sideways on phones.
Error messages in the analyzer and in Find the best AI are now shown in your language.
Under PT, the home page says that the headlines are in English.
Security: usage limits on the analysis endpoints and stricter response headers.
Promptea now speaks Brazilian Portuguese: pick PT in the header. The interface, the product pages, the glossary, the model pages and the prompt packs are translated.
The analyzer answers in Portuguese: score, findings, recommendations and the optimized prompt. A prompt written in Portuguese is analyzed properly from any language of the site.
Find the best AI explains its recommendation in Portuguese too.
AI Daily and the newsletter are still written in English and Spanish: under PT they are shown in English, and the page says so.
The 58 prompting guides are translated into Portuguese too.
Image prompts requested in Portuguese are composed in English around your own words, which is what image generators understand best.

A new home page that explains itself at a glance: what Promptea does, the two things you can do (analyze a prompt, find the best AI) and the box to paste your prompt, which now says what you get back.
One menu for the whole site, in the same place on every page, with a compact version on phones.
New page “How Promptea works”: how a prompt is scored, which AIs are supported, the FAQ and the product tour.
Benchmarks: the ranking no longer overlaps on any screen, phones no longer scroll sideways, and a new chart shows which providers are in the top of each benchmark.
The prompt you paste on the home page no longer travels in the address bar on its way to the analyzer.
The newsletter card opens by itself only on your first visit, without blocking the page; after that it stays as a small pill.
The background moves a little more; if your system asks for reduced motion it stays still.
Fixes: the analyzer works with browser storage blocked, weekly editions show their real label, and the footer shows the right version.
Prompt engine: a before → after score for the optimized prompt, better handling of every prompt type, and an optional second AI provider so the optimizer keeps working when one is down.
Benchmarks with charts: top models per benchmark, price vs. score, a frontier matrix and a cost calculator.
A prompt library saved only in your browser, and a shareable card with your score (never the prompt text).
Brand: the mascot is now the favicon and the social card, and it hops when you hover or tap it. The feedback dialog no longer shows the page through it.
About and Methodology pages, a larger glossary and deeper guides.
Easier to find and cite: structured data on every page, llms.txt and a plain-text version of each guide for AI assistants.

flow.title: Prompt flow
flow.subtitle: Write a big task and we split it into steps: a chain of ready-to-paste prompts, with parallel branches and the AI that fits each one best.
flow.placeholder: E.g.: Launch a weekly newsletter for my design studio: define the audience, write the first issue and build a sign-up page.
examples: Add Google sign-in to my Next.js app and cover it with tests
Write a sales proposal for a client who wants to redesign their online store
Compare three CRMs for a 10-person company and recommend one with reasons

notices.no_ai: AI isn't available right now, so this is the basic plan from Promptea's engine. It works the same way: every step has its prompt ready.
notices.budget: The AI allowance for this period is used up, so this is the basic plan from Promptea's engine. AI comes back on its own when the allowance renews.
notices.quota: You've used today's AI flows. This is the basic plan from Promptea's engine; AI flows are back tomorrow.
notices.busy: The AI is in high demand right now. Here is the basic plan; try again in a while.
notices.error: The AI didn't return a usable plan, so here is the basic plan from Promptea's engine.

how: The main task is at the top; below it, the steps in the order they are best done. Steps on the same row don't depend on each other: you can run them at the same time, in separate chats.
Every step comes with a ready-to-paste prompt. Where it says [Output of step N], paste what that step gave you.
The AI suggested for each step is picked by the same engine as "Find the best AI", with its reason. You can take any step to the analyzer to improve it.
Claude (Anthropic) writes the plan. When AI isn't available, Promptea's engine builds a basic plan that works just as well. Promptea doesn't store your task.

content.text.title: Text without JavaScript
content.text.body: Most agents read the HTML and never run scripts. The page's text has to be there when it arrives.

content.semantics.title: Semantic outline
content.semantics.body: One h1, ordered headings, a main landmark and a language: how an agent finds the part that answers the question.

content.meta.title: Title, description, canonical
content.meta.body: What an agent shows when it lists the page, and the URL it should cite.

content.weight.title: HTML weight
content.weight.body: Every byte of HTML costs the agent tokens. Heavy pages push the content out of its context.

markdown.negotiation.title: Markdown on request
markdown.negotiation.body: Answering Accept: text/markdown with markdown gives agents the same page for a fraction of the tokens.

markdown.twin.title: Markdown twin (.md)
markdown.twin.body: A stable .md URL per page: a clean document to fetch and something worth linking from llms.txt.

markdown.alternate.title: Markdown announced
markdown.alternate.body: A link in the head or a Link header tells the agent the markdown version exists.

structured.jsonld.title: Valid JSON-LD
structured.jsonld.body: Structured data states facts (who, what, price, date) so the agent does not have to infer them from prose.

structured.types.title: The right schema.org types
structured.types.body: The type that matches the page (Article, Product, FAQPage…) is what lets an agent answer a specific question from it.

structured.social.title: Open Graph
structured.social.body: The fallback metadata many agents read when there is no JSON-LD: title, description and image.

api.catalog.title: API catalog
api.catalog.body: /.well-known/api-catalog is where an agent learns the site has an API, without guessing URLs.

api.openapi.title: OpenAPI description
api.openapi.body: Paths, parameters and response shapes, so an agent calls the API right the first time.

api.mcp.title: MCP server, discoverable
api.mcp.body: MCP is how agents use a product instead of only reading about it. A catalog lets them find the server from the domain.

api.webmcp.title: WebMCP on the page
api.webmcp.body: Lets a browser agent call the page's actions as tools. An early Chrome proposal; read statically here.

api.skills.title: Agent skills index
api.skills.body: Packaged instructions that tell coding agents how to work with the product.

bots.robots.title: robots.txt
bots.robots.body: The first file every well-behaved crawler and agent reads: rules, signals and the sitemap live there.

bots.ai-rules.title: Rules for AI agents
bots.ai-rules.body: Blocking the bots that act for a person makes the site unreadable to assistants. Refusing training crawlers is your call and costs nothing here.

bots.signals.title: Content Signals
bots.signals.body: Say what fetched content may be used for: search, answering a user, training.

discovery.sitemap.title: Sitemap
discovery.sitemap.body: The complete list of what the site wants read, instead of URLs guessed from links.

discovery.links.title: Link headers
discovery.links.body: Tell an agent where the machine-readable resources are before it parses a byte of HTML.

discovery.llms.title: llms.txt
discovery.llms.body: A short markdown index of the pages worth reading. Cheap to add; evidence that agents fetch it on their own is still thin, so it weighs little.

connect.title: Let your agent fix it
connect.lead: This audit is saved. Connect your coding agent to it in one step: it reads the findings, follows your plan and implements each fix in your repo, with an acceptance check per fix.
connect.claudeHint: Run this in your project's folder, then ask Claude Code: “Implement the Promptea audit”.
connect.codexHint: Add this to ~/.codex/config.toml, then ask Codex to implement the Promptea audit.
connect.cursorHint: Add this to .cursor/mcp.json in your project, or install it with the button.
steps: Your agent reads the audit and your plan.
It implements each fix and runs its acceptance check.
After you deploy, it re-scans and the score here updates.
connect.secret: The address includes this audit's private id. Share it only with your own agent.
connect.noSession: This audit could not be saved, so there is nothing to connect to. You can still copy the fixes as a prompt.
connect.fallbackTitle: No MCP? Copy it as a prompt
connect.fallbackBody: The same fixes, in your plan's order, as one markdown prompt to paste into any AI.
connect.services: Rather have someone do it? eterlab, the studio behind Promptea, implements it for you.

how: Promptea fetches the page the way an agent does: no JavaScript, plus the files agents look for (robots.txt, sitemap, llms.txt, API and MCP catalogs).
21 checks run on what came back. They are deterministic rules: the same site gets the same score, and no AI decides it.
You see the page next to what an agent reads from it, and you arrange the findings into a fix plan.
The audit is saved for 14 days. Your coding agent connects to it through Promptea's MCP server and implements the plan in your repo.
agentReady.weightsBody: The 100 points lean toward what agents demonstrably use today: text that exists without JavaScript, markdown, structured data, and APIs or MCP. llms.txt is worth 3 points, because evidence that agents read it on their own is still thin.

faq.a: That an AI agent sent to your site can read it cheaply, understand what it states, and find what it can do there: an API, an MCP server, a form. Agents are becoming visitors in their own right, and most of them do not run JavaScript or look at layout.
No. The checks are deterministic rules that run on Promptea's server over what your site returns. The same site gets the same score every time.

faq.q: What does my coding agent do with the audit?
faq.a: It connects to Promptea's MCP server with the address shown after the scan. From there it reads the findings, gets each fix with the files and code for your stack, implements it in your repository, checks it, and marks it done. After you deploy, it can scan again.

The audit of the public page you scanned, your fix plan and which fixes are done, for 14 days. No account, no email, no IP address. Anyone with the audit's link can see it, so share the link only with people or agents you trust.
